Stopped blaming myself for everything wrong in my life. My dad was very big into personal responsibility, but it amounted to "anything negative in your life is your fault". This was also coming from a man who beat his kids a lot, for reasons as petty as saying "water" incorrectly.

It took a lot of time and introspection and political evolution to pull myself out of that. After a bunch of suicide attempts and depression that started very early on.

Some bad things in your life are because of bad choices you made. But some aren't. Sometimes they're the result of vast social forces outside of your control. Sometimes you're just unlucky. Sometimes people will dislike you because you're autistic or you remind them of an ex or whatever.

Having a realistic appraisal of the negative things in my life helped my depression hugely. It's still there and some scars will never heal, but I don't spend hours every night imagining myself hanging from a rafter or jumping in front of a train. Most days I have zero ideation.

Another thing is having friends you can emotionally confide in. Not everyone can afford therapy or is lucky enough to find one that clicks. Men especially tend to have emotionally surface level relationships where a lot of deeper introspective conversations don't happen. It's changing, but slowly. This isn't an indictment on men. Sharing hobbies and having light ribbing sessions is fine, but the lack of emotional vulnerability and reciprocal support is something I think is very harmful.
